title: Taurine levels modulate aging | Nature Aging
abstract:
More recently, studies have reported that taurine concentrations decline naturally with age in some organs, which raises the possibility that the drop in taurine may contribute to physiological decline with aging.

Taurine first garnered attention in companion animals such as cats and dogs, whose endogenous taurine production is very low or absent, explains corresponding author of the study Vijay Yadav.
The public, mostly the affluent subset, came together and provided the impetus to identify why their cats were visibly growth-retarded and blind. In a seminal study published in Science in 1975, Hayes, Carey and Schmidt showed that retinal degeneration in cats is caused by the lack in the processed diets of a single molecule, taurine”.
